title: C++ and RPC file handle seek error behavior
scope: forkfs::Namespace::seek negative computed positions return EINVAL
forkfs::Namespace::seek positions above INT64_MAX return EOVERFLOW
daemon raw fs-hseek RPC maps those system errors to the corresponding wire codes
Rejected seeks preserve the shared open-description cursor, file content, inode metadata, and committed sequence
explicit_exclusions: Native lseek(2) behavior is kernel-controlled and is not validated by this record
No new mount capability is claimed

cpp_regression.observed: The added negative seek assertion received a generic exception ('negative file position') rather than std::system_error.

raw_rpc_regression.observed: Negative fs-hseek SET returned generic wire code 1 instead of the EINVAL wire code 23.

fixed_validation.execution: Disposable no-Git archive; runtime and tests matched the recorded source hashes. macOS 27.2.1 arm64, Apple Clang/SDK 27.2, Release, FSKit enabled; deny-default sandbox excluded home, keychain, credentials, and publishing paths; loopback-only tests.

source_review.scope: Typed seek-domain errors only; invalid C++ seek enum behavior retained. Raw RPC exercises existing system_error-to-errno mapping. No general RPC mapping or parser changes.

native_apfs_reference.role: independent native syscall context only; not forkfs regression or mount evidence
